thread:
Priya (customer): hey, we started getting a ton of 400s from the charge endpoint ~10m ago and a billing surge. stack trace shows fncall schema error. link to logs: https://redwood.logs/acct/9876 :worried:
Mia (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the failing request payload and the exact API response? we'll escalate if it's repro'd in prod :thumbsup:
Priya (customer): here's a sanitized snippet — occurs when model returns a function call: ```POST /v1/call_tool
{ 
  "tool": "charge-tool",
  "args": "charge $1200 to acct 4321"
}
Response: 400 "invalid JSON schema for args"
```
Mia (Support): hm args should be JSON not humanized strings. did this start after the doc update or a model change? any recent prompt changes? :thinking_face:
Priya (customer): No infra deploys on our side. We did update the system prompt examples yesterday to show a 'natural language' user example for payments. Could that break function calling?
Jordan (Eng): possible — if the system prompt includes fewshot examples that show humanized arguments, some models will pattern-match and emit strings instead of proper JSON args. can you share the system prompt snippet?
Priya (customer): pasted below (redacted): ```System: You are a helpful assistant. Example: User: "Charge my card for $1,200" Assistant calls charge-tool with args: "charge $1,200 to acct 4321"```
Jordan (Eng): yeah that's the culprit. the example is shadowing the tool schema and teaching the model to output a human string as fn args. our function-caller routing then chooses charge-tool because the example uses that tool name. that causes schema validation errors at the tool gateway. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
Sahil (ML): confirming — ran a quick local prompt with the same example and model variant and got identical behavior: model emits function name "charge-tool" with args as a plain string. quick repro: ```input: system+user as above -> model output: {
  "name": "charge-tool",
  "arguments": "charge $1,200 to acct 4321"
}```
Jordan (Eng): immediate mitigation: 1) add a validation layer at our gateway to reject non-JSON fn args and return a clear 422 to customer (we already have schema checks but temporarily relax auto-forwarding). 2) deploy a routing rule to pin this customer to model-variant v1-safe (less fewshot generalization) while we patch examples. 3) ask customer to rollback the example changes — simplest fix.
Mia (Support): I'll propose those to the customer. Priya, do you want us to revert your system prompt example or apply a temporary API rule on your org? we can also set a quota to stop billing spiral.
Priya (customer): please revert the example ASAP and enable temporary quota. also would appreciate a quick patch on our account to reject malformed args so we don't get charged for retries.
deploy-bot: [automation] created ticket CS-9321 (priority P1) for prompt-induced fncall schema failures; linked to infra incident #4578
Sahil (ML): small fix for future: enforce that fewshot examples use the exact tool arg JSON shape (e.g., {"amount_cents":120000,"account_id":4321}) instead of natural language. we should also add a linter rule in the DevEx repo that flags examples using plain text in tool args.
Jordan (Eng): logged a quick PR for gateway validation: reject non-JSON function args and return friendly error + event to billing so we can pause charges on malformed retries. merging to staging now.
Mia (Support): updating customer: we've created CS-9321, asked for example rollback, applied temporary quota and started a routing pin to v1-safe. we'll confirm once PR is live. will follow up with root-cause postmortem. :eyes:
Priya (customer): thanks team, that timeline works. please mark any followups against my org id 9876.
Jordan (Eng): FYI, added a note to add a docs entry: "Examples that show tool usage must use the tool's JSON schema — never natural language."
Mia (Support): action items: revert example (customer), quota applied (support), gateway validation PR (eng), linter rule (devex), postmortem (eng-sre). I'll close P1 once customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
Priya (customer): confirmed after revert — errors stopped and billing spike stabilized. will expect follow-up postmortem.
Mia (Support): great — closing loop here. thanks everyone! :tada:
